data: Last successful Soviet Moon mission — returned 170 g of Mare Crisium regolith 1976-08-22; last lunar sample return until Chang'e 5

The last successful Soviet Moon mission and the last sample-return lunar lander until Chang'e 5 in 2020 — a 44-year gap. Launched 1976-08-09 from Baikonur on a Proton-K, Luna 24 soft-landed in Mare Crisium (12.7° N, 62.2° E) on 1976-08-18, drilled to a depth of 2.25 m using its rotary-percussive drill, retrieved a 1.6 m core sample, and lifted off the ascent stage which returned 170.1 g of lunar regolith to western Siberia (~200 km southeast of Surgut) on 1976-08-22. Soviet scientists at the Vernadsky Institute confirmed the presence of water (~0.1 % by mass) in the samples in a 1978 paper that was largely ignored in the West until LCROSS and Chandrayaan-1 (2008-09) re-confirmed lunar water.
Akhmanova et al. (1978) — water in Luna 24 regolith (Geokhimiia)
Soviet 1973 Mars lander — first descent telemetry from Mars atmosphere (224 s, mostly corrupted)
First human-made object to reach Mars surface; lander crashed (1971)
First soft landing on Mars; 14.5 s of surface transmission
First colour images of the Venusian surface — survived 127 minutes in 457 °C / 89-atm conditions
First soft landing on another planet and first to transmit data from another planet's surface (Venus, 1970)

The last Soviet lunar mission — and the last uncrewed Moon landing until China's Chang'e 3 in 2013: a gap of 37 years. Returned 170 g of samples including minerals containing water, foreshadowing the later discovery of lunar water ice.
